audit_item: A04 / reject circular JSON data in project research registry
finding: The shared registry JSON validator recursively traversed dict/list/tuple values without tracking active containers. Separately, strict persisted JSON decoding leaked RecursionError for sufficiently deep documents instead of returning its stable malformed-data error.
change: Serialization validation now uses iterative depth-first traversal and rejects cycles. Strict JSON decoding normalizes decoder RecursionError to ValueError for unsupported nesting depth.

verification.red_reproduction: A self-referential list triggered recursive key validation; a 20,000-level JSON array triggered Python 3.14 json.decoder RecursionError.
verification.registry_and_all_package_json_helpers: tests/test_research_access.py tests/test_strict_json_constants.py with RouteB packages/*/src explicitly first on PYTHONPATH: 146 passed
verification.ruff: passed for all seven package json_utils.py modules, access.py, and both test files
verification.mypy: passed for all seven package json_utils.py modules and access.py

boundary: The regression used a temporary registry and synthetic cyclic Python objects only; no project registry, market data, account export, or formal evaluation record was accessed.
